facts.statement: Proardea is an extinct genus of heron that includes the species Proardea amissa and Proardea? deschutteri.
facts.quote: Proardea is an extinct genus of heron, containing two species, Proardea amissa ("lost proto-heron") and Proardea? deschutteri from the Borgloon Formation of Belgium.

facts.statement: Proardea stood approximately 70 cm (2 ft 4 in) tall and had a body shape very similar to modern herons.
facts.quote: It stood about 70 cm (2 ft 4 in) tall and was very similar to a modern heron in shape.

facts.statement: Fossils of Proardea have been found in fragmentary form in Quercy, France, with dated remains from the Late Oligocene at Pech Desse, though the original fossil may date back to the Late Eocene.
facts.quote: The species is known from rather fragmentary fossils in the area of Quercy, France; dated remains are from Pech Desse, a Late Oligocene locality, but the original fossil, a single right tarsometatarsus (MNHN QU-15720), isn't precisely dated and may have come from deposits as early as Late Eocene in age.

facts.statement: Proardea is classified as being closely related to the subfamily Ardeinae, which includes true herons and egrets.
facts.quote: Proardea was apparently closely related to the true herons and egrets (Ardeinae).

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that Proardea may have been a direct ancestor of modern herons and egrets because related genera only appear in the fossil record from the Miocene onwards.
facts.quote: As these genera are only known from the Miocene onwards, Proardea possibly was a direct ancestor of today's herons and/or egrets.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the Miocene genus Proardeola is synonymous with Proardea, with some researchers suggesting Proardeola walkeri might be identical to Proardea amissa.
facts.quote: However, the Miocene genus Proardeola is closely related, or perhaps even synonymous, with Proardea; the former's single species Proardeola walkeri may thus be Proardea walkeri or even identical with P. amissa.

facts.statement: The parent group for the genus Proardea is Ardeinae.
Proardea belongs to the family Ardeidae.
Proardea lived during the Rupelian stage, approximately 33.9 to 27.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Rupelian to Rupelian (33.9 to 27.3 million years ago)

facts.statement: The genus Proardea was described by Lambrecht in 1933.
The type species of the genus Proardea is Proardea amissa.
Proardea amissa was previously known by the synonyms Ardea amissa and Egretta amissa.

rejected.statement: Proardea is classified within the class Aves.
